reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an instructional walkthrough for creating a YouTube channel, uploading videos, and using account or upload settings. Although it mentions earning money, it does not describe a guaranteed return, fee, investment, or unusual participation condition. The engagement prompts and references to channel creation, privacy, tags, and verification are ordinary YouTube functions.

I'm going to tell you how to create a YouTube channel with your phone.
You can see how the video is uploaded
So write all the words that are in the tags.
you can recover from an alternate email ID

opening.argument: The central pitch links a simple viewer action to an income outcome. The speaker says viewers can create a channel, upload videos, and then “make money,” while the title presents creating a mobile channel and earning online as one combined proposition. That makes the channel-creation workflow more than neutral technical instruction: it is presented as the route to a financial benefit. The video does not establish what conditions, eligibility requirements, effort, or realistic limitations apply before money can be earned. A low-barrier action is therefore paired with an inadequately qualified income promise.

citations.quote: how to create a channel on YouTube, how to upload videos, and how to make your own channel. So, guys, you can make money.
How to Create Youtube Channel in Mobile and Earn Money Online

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the steps ordinary YouTube functions does not answer the promotional linkage. The referenced upload and tagging instructions are the mechanism viewers are told to use, while the opening frames that mechanism as a way to earn money. The absence of a stated fee does not remove the financial inducement or show that the outcome is realistically qualified.

citations.quote: You can see how the video is uploaded

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The income wording does not promise that merely creating a channel guarantees payment. The actual walkthrough explains account creation, uploading, tags, privacy, recovery, and verification, and it does not request a deposit, purchase, or payment. Linking channel operation with possible earnings is ordinary creator education, not proof of a scam.

citations.quote: I'm going to tell you how to create a YouTube channel with your phone.
public means that your video can be viewed by anyone
Verify is very easy

opening.argument: Several financial and solicitation signals reinforce one another. The title foregrounds earning money online, the description separately advertises a video about how much YouTube pays for 1,000 views, and viewers are repeatedly directed to subscribe and visit linked channel resources. That combination can make the offer appear easy and actionable without showing the basis for the claimed earnings or the conditions for receiving them. The content supplies a participation path and promotional links, but not evidence that ordinary viewers will obtain the advertised financial result.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the links concern a YouTube channel does not make the earnings framing harmless. The description puts payment-related material beside explicit subscription and visit directions, so the viewer is steered toward participation before the video establishes realistic earning conditions. Ordinary-looking links can still function as acquisition and promotion when paired with an income message.

citations.quote: How to Earn money from Youtube Channel
For next video Subscribe our Channel by clicking the link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not evidence of a hidden payment or withdrawal scheme. The listed material is about YouTube creation and earnings generally, while the requested actions are subscribing, visiting a channel, and learning. No fee, deposit, guaranteed amount, or unusual verification demand is shown; the payment-related title alone cannot establish deception.

opening.argument: The tutorial format also operates as channel promotion. It tells viewers how to create and optimize a channel, presents earning money as the payoff, and then directs them to subscribe, visit the channel, and use linked templates and related resources. The instructional details give the promotion credibility, but the overall viewer journey ends in channel participation and continued engagement. That makes the apparent education a recruitment funnel for a low-effort income proposition, even though the video does not demonstrate an actual earning result or explain meaningful limits.

citations.quote: So, guys, you can make money.
Youtube Channel Template : http://bit.ly/2IRjCkx
Visit our Channel : https://www.youtube.com/StudyChannel
like the video, share the video of all your friends, subscribe to the channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational wrapper is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive: concrete setup instructions can normalize the promised route to income. The closing calls to like, share, and subscribe are not needed to explain account settings; they show the video is also steering audience growth. The technical subject therefore does not rule out promotional solicitation.

citations.quote: subscribe to the channel, press the bell icon
Share, Support, Subscribe

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The calls to subscribe and use templates promote the creator, but promotion is not itself a scam. The demonstrated workflow remains a recognizable YouTube setup tutorial: viewers create a channel, choose visibility, add tags, and verify it. The material does not show that viewers must pay, recruit others, or surrender funds to obtain income.
